Markings of a table

Source: R/results.R
soil_markings.Rd

Every marking of a wide read as a long data frame: the raw markings of the cells (cell_markings: value_count, methods_differ, value_spread, source_method_kind, method_facets of WoSIS cells listing several values), of the layers (texture_sum, consistency_flags), of the profiles (also_in_datasets, possible_profile, superseded_by, and with layer = "first" the profile_markings), the retirement of cells (retired_cells) and, with view = "revised", the revised markings of the horizons, of the cells and the values a revised rule did not return (hidden_values). Markings change no row and no value: they describe them.

Usage

soil_markings(x)

Arguments

x

A soil_table. Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A data frame row (row number in x), horizon_id, scope ("cell", "layer", "profile", "retired_cell", "revised_horizon", "revised_cell", "hidden_value"), column (the variable column, or the source property code of a hidden value; NA for a row marking), marking (the marking name, or the rule of a hidden value) and value (character).

Details

A marking holding several values gives one row per value; an object (such as method_facets) gives one row with its JSON text.

In the long layout the cell markings are columns of the row (column is its property_code), the layer and profile markings repeat on every observation of the horizon, and revised_markings mixes the horizon markings with those of the cell (texture_normalized, guessed_elements_removed, value_from_estimates, kept_from_copy, values_differ: scope "revised_cell").

See also

Other results: soil_columns(), soil_first_layer(), soil_flags(), soil_metadata(), soil_revised_rules(), soil_table

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
m <- soil_markings(x)
m[m$scope == "hidden_value", ]
} # }
